newsitem.title: ITALY: Thousands watch re-run of Foucault's pendulum test.
newsitem.headline: Thousands watch re-run of Foucault's pendulum test.

text.p: Around 8,000 people packed Florence cathedral for a re-run of French scientist Jean Foucault's famous pendulum experiment in 1851 that proved the earth rotates on its own axis.
Italian author Umberto Eco, whose second novel was entitled "Foucault's Pendulum", attended the event on Thursday night as part of the cathedral's 700th anniversary celebrations.
"The pendulum is magical and it's a magical evening because of the place chosen for the experiment," Eco said.
Foucault proved that the earth rotated by suspending a 28-kg (62-lb) lead ball from a wire 67 metres (222 feet) long at the Pantheon in Paris.
The experiment proves the earth turns on its own axis because the pendulum slowly oscillates as it swings.
The Florence event recreated Foucault's experiment with an 89-kg (196-lb) weight suspended from an 88-metre (294 feet) wire attached to Brunelleschi's famous frescoed dome.
